topic: Fundamentals of Vectors and Linear Algebra

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors and Linear Algebra

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
sections.content: Define vectors as entities possessing both magnitude and direction, contrasted with scalars (magnitude only). Introduce the coordinate plane representation (x, y).
sections.example: A GPS-guided drone flying 5km North (vector) versus a drone's battery level at 80% (scalar).

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Explain vector addition geometrically. Visualize the result as the diagonal of a parallelogram. Introduce the concept of resultant vectors.
sections.example: A cat walking 3 meters East, then 4 meters North. The 'resultant' path is the straight-line displacement from the start to the end point.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping
sections.content: Discuss how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its length or reverses its direction. Use a scaling factor (k) to show visual compression or expansion.
sections.example: A game character running at velocity V. If they get a 'Speed Boost' power-up, their velocity becomes 2V (doubling the vector length).

sections.title: Linear Combinations: Spanning the Space
sections.content: Explain that any vector in 2D can be reached by a combination of two basis vectors (i and j). Introduce the concept of linear span.
sections.example: A robotic arm with two joints; by adjusting the lengths (scalars) of its segments (basis vectors), the gripper can reach any point in its reachable workspace.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Briefly recap vectors as the building blocks of Linear Algebra. Conclude by mentioning how these concepts form the foundation for 3D graphics and AI neural networks.
sections.example: Visualizing how pixels on a screen are essentially vectors being transformed and manipulated by matrix operations to render animations.

storyboard.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
lecture_lines: Vectors have both magnitude and direction.
Scalars possess only magnitude, like numbers.
Vectors are represented in a coordinate plane.
animations: Fade in vector 'v' as a directed arrow from origin. Label 'v' in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the arrow 'v' in #FF0000 to emphasize its components.
Draw horizontal/vertical components with dashed lines in #00FF00. Label 'x' and 'y'.
Animate the vector 'v' moving to a new coordinate point.
Flash the final components in #FFFF00 for emphasis.

storyboard.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
lecture_lines: Add vectors by connecting them tip-to-tail.
The resultant vector connects start to end.
Addition forms the diagonal of a parallelogram.
animations: Draw two vectors 'v' and 'w' from the origin. Label in #FFFFFF.
Slide vector 'w' so its tail touches the tip of 'v'.
Draw resultant vector 'v+w' from origin to new tip. Color #00FFFF.

storyboard.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping
lecture_lines: Negative scalars reverse a vector's direction.
Multiplying stretches or compresses the vector.
animations: Show scaling factor 'c=2' stretching 'v' to twice length. Label '2v' in #00FF00.
Show scaling factor 'c=-1' flipping 'v' to opposite direction. Label '-v' in #FF0000.

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations: Spanning the Space
lecture_lines: Any vector can reach any coordinate point.
We use basis vectors i and j.
animations: Draw two basis vectors 'i' and 'j' in #FFFFFF. Label.
Show '2i' stretching 'i' and '3j' stretching 'j'. Label in #00FF00.
Draw the diagonal vector sum as the linear combination. Label in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Summary and Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Vectors are foundational to linear algebra.
Vectors drive modern AI neural networks.
animations: Fade in key summary points: Vectors, Addition, Scaling, Spans. Label in #FFFFFF.
Show a 3D robot arm moving representing vector transformation. Label in #00FFFF.
Flash 'Vector Algebra' heading in #FFFF00 to conclude.
